sections.title: Condition Filter [Export JIOrder method]
paragraphs: Condition filters allow the identification of a subset of orders matching certain criteria.
A same condition filter can be expressed more than once. All specified filters are requested to be matched (they are all applied in AND clause).
For instance, it is possible to apply the following filters:
The result will be that all Order having creation date greater than 2011-11-20 AND lower than 2012-01-20 (between 2011-11-20 AND 2012-01-20) will be retrieved.
Condition filters are also available server side as restrictive conditions. The filter conditions entered client side will be joined with the filter conditions configured server side.

It is possible to enable the component filters according to particular values of the condition filters server side. By this way, it is possible to configure different chains, everyone with different restrictive conditions and therefore with different subsets of component filters enabled.

For instance, based on the specific configuration set up for the single integration, will be possible to allow the webservice client to export only order belonging to a certain workflow step, even if this filter is not set by the integration client.

sections.title: Saving Attachment
paragraphs: If the name of an attachment in the PO validation response document is identical to the name of an existing attachment, the new attachment replaces the existing attachment.
The matching process is case-sensitive and includes the file extension.
For example, Hello.doc is not identical to and would not replace hello.doc, and Goodbye.doc is not identical to and would not replace Goodbye.pdf.
The PO validation response document supports .p7m files (application/pkcs7-mime), a type of encrypted mime file.

sections.title: Adding a new PO
paragraphs: There are two ways to add a new PO to the eProcurement solution.
Set the operationCode in the PO Header element to new.
Omit the operationCode attribute and the revisionNumber field from the PO Header element. If you do so, the eProcurement solution manages the PO request as a new PO.
The eProcurement solution creates a new PO if the PONumber and CreateDateTime fields are not present in the POHeader element, or when your organization allows duplicate POs.

sections.title: Updating fields in an existing PO
paragraphs: You can update the following header-level fields in the PO Header:
Billing options (accounting date, payment terms, FOB)
Delivery options (expedite, ship via, requested delivery date)
Custom fields (account codes, buyer, and so on)
You can update the following line-level fields in the PO Line:
Split and non-split custom fields (account codes, buyer, and so on)
The eProcurement solution matches existing PO lines based on the value of the linenumber attribute. The solution updates a line in the PO Line element if either of the following conditions occurs:
The operationCode attribute in the PO Line element is set to update.

The operationCode attribute is not present in the PO Line element, the linenumber attribute matches an existing PO Line, and the Quantity field is not set to zero (0). (If the Quantity field is set to zero, the eProcurement solution marks the line as cancelled.)
The eProcurement solution rejects the update when one or more of the following conditions occur:
The PONumber field is not present in the POHeader element.
The PONumber and the CreateDateTime fields match more than one PO.
The PO has already been closed, cancelled, or rejected.
Your organization allows duplicate POs and the PO update request matches more than one existing PO.

sections.title: Adding a line
paragraphs: The eProcurement solution adds a new line to the POLine element if either of the following conditions occurs:
The operationCode attribute in the PO Line element is set to new.

The operationCode attribute is not present in the PO Line element, the linenumber attribute does not match an existing PO Line, and the Quantity field is not set to zero (0). (If the Quantity field is set to zero, the eProcurement solution marks the line as cancelled.)

sections.title: Cancelling a line
paragraphs: The eProcurement solution cancels an existing line in the POLine element if one or more of the following conditions occur:
The operationCode attribute in the POLine element is set to cancel.

The operationCode attribute is not present in the PO Line element, the linenumber attribute matches an existing PO Line, and the Quantity field is set to zero (0). Note that in order to use the zero-quantity cancellation method, you must enable Allow Zero Quantity in the PO.
The operationCode attribute is not present in the POLine element, the linenumber attribute matches an existing POLine, and the status attribute of the SupplierStatus field is set to cancel.

sections.title: Cancelling an entire PO
paragraphs: There are two ways to cancel an entire PO.
Set the operationCode attribute in the POHeader element to cancel.
Cancel all of the lines in the PO.
The eProcurement solution rejects the cancellation request if one or more of the following conditions occur:
The PONumber and CreateDateTime fields cannot be found in the eProcurement solution.
Your organization allows duplicate POs and the PO cancellation request matches more than one existing PO.

sections.title: Attachment
paragraphs: The PO import document supports header-level attachments in the InternalInfo and ExternalInfo element for new POs. The total number and size of attachments must not exceed the maximum specified for the organization.
If you are using the PO import document to update the PO, header-level attachments are not supported.

sections.title: Behaviour [JIOrder Status Import method]
paragraphs: A single request of PO status import method can contain also more than one PO status information, and all POs statuses are imported sequentially.
There are some limitation and things that must be taken in account when inserting more than one “JIPoStatus [JIOrder Status Import method]” object.

sections.title: General note on PO Status Import feature
paragraphs: When an error occurs, the import is stopped. All POs prior to the error are imported successfully; the PO message for which the error occurred, and any following PO messages are not imported.

That can make it difficult to determine which POs imported successfully and which did not. Therefore, unless you are batching hundreds of transactions, we recommend that you include no more than one PO in your PO status import document.

Each status request can include only one reference to a given PO. For example, it is not possible to send an open status and a closed status for the same PO on a single status message. Doing so will cause the import to fail.
